ShortDescription.Value: Draw an area and get a whole neighbourhood: streets that follow the hill, or a grid, rings or a fan on flat ground, with level lots, zoning and service buildings. Preview it, reroll it, build it.

Publish.LongDescription:
Building on hills in Cities: Skylines II is slow and fiddly. Stepped Streets does it for you: draw an area on a hillside and it lays out a whole neighbourhood the way a careful builder would. Already have streets? **Use existing** zones them with your own zone mix, without new roads.
### What it builds
- **Streets that follow the contours**, so they stay nearly level along the hill - **Gentle connectors** that climb across the slope, never steeper than the grade you set (8 % by default) - **A connection to your nearest road** within 400 m, or a neighbourhood of its own when there is none - **Level lots stepped down the hill** with soft banks, graded before anything is zoned - **Zoning that grows**: the game's own zone cells along the new roads, as deep as each levelled lot, in the mix you choose (or none, to zone the lots yourself) - **Zoning for streets you already have**: pick **Use existing**, draw around them, and their empty zone cells get your mix (Random, Clumps or Even, zone packs included), with no new roads and no ground changes; cells you zoned yourself stay as they are - **Service buildings** mixed in: police, fire, clinics and hospitals, schools, parks, utilities, any unlocked roadside service building, each on a level site of its own facing the road - **Trees if you want them**: forest on ground too steep to build and trees on the banks (off by default), optional garden walls
### How to use it
1. Click **Stepped Streets** in the bottom toolbar beside Zones, or press **Ctrl+Shift+S**. 2. Click corners on the ground; click the first corner to close the area. Drag corners to reshape, right-click removes one, Ctrl+Z undoes. 3. Pick **Build new** and a **layout**, or **Use existing** for streets you already have; then **what to build**: zones with their shares and services with how many of each. 4. The plan appears on the ground. **Reroll** for another layout. 5. Press **Build** (it says **Zone** for existing streets).
**Layouts**: Contour suburb, Terraced blocks and Mountain lane follow the hill. Nine grids suit flat or gentle ground (Square, Rectangular, Irregular, Skewed, Fragmented, Curved, Warped, Diagonal avenues and Radial grid), with **crossroads**, **staggered** T-junctions or a **traffic**-optimised through road. Star, Rings, Spiderweb and Fan spread streets from a centre. Spine, Ladder, Comb, Fishbone, Tree, Cul-de-sacs, Loops, Loops and lollipops, and Lollipops on a stick run trunk streets in from your road with side streets off them. Triangular mesh, Hexagonal and Hexagons with spokes tile the area; Ridge and Valley put a main road along the crest or the valley floor; Coastal follows the shore; Winding is one long road back and forth. Organic mesh, Hybrid, Polycentric, Superblock, Radburn, Fused grid, Filtered grid and Barcelona superblock follow planners' models. Everything but the three hillside layouts is new and marked experimental until it has been built in more cities. Untick **Shape the ground** to leave the terrain exactly as it is.
Turn on **Steep hills** for steep slopes and mountain sides. Everything else (road type, block depth, grades, lot size, grading, trees) is under **More settings**.
### Good to know
- **Ground changes are permanent**, like the game's terrain tools. **Back up your save** before a big build. - Houses grow where the city has demand for that zone. - Big areas (up to 6.4 km across) take a while to plan and lay a lot of road at once. - Early release: expect rough edges and tell me what you find.
Built for game version **1.6.***.
### Credits
Parts of the build code are adapted from **Placemaker** by jackwrichards (GPL-3.0), which in turn credits ParkManager and Grid Road Generator. Stepped Streets is GPL-3.0 too; the full source is on GitHub (link on this page).
